title: How often?
goal: Say how often you do things with toujours, souvent, parfois, rarement and ne… jamais, and talk about regular days like le lundi.

blocks.title: At a community centre in Moncton
blocks.context: Amira, a volunteer, is doing a short survey about daily habits. She talks to Raj.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.en: Hello, Raj! Do you cook often?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Oui, je cuisine tous les jours.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Et le soir, vous regardez la télé ?
lines.en: And in the evening, do you watch TV?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Rarement. Le soir, j'écoute souvent la radio.
lines.en: Rarely. In the evening, I often listen to the radio.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Parfois. Mais je ne travaille jamais le dimanche !
lines.en: Sometimes. But I never work on Sundays!

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.en: Do you go to bed late?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Non, je me couche toujours à 22 heures. Mais la fin de semaine, je me couche quelquefois à minuit.
lines.en: No, I always go to bed at 10 p.m. But on weekends, I sometimes go to bed at midnight.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.fr: Et vous avez un cours de français ?
lines.en: And do you have a French class?

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Oui, une fois par semaine, le mercredi. Et lundi, j'ai un examen !
lines.en: Yes, once a week, on Wednesdays. And this Monday, I have an exam!

blocks.body: Look at the last line: [[le mercredi]] means *every Wednesday*, but [[lundi]] with no article means *this Monday*. You will see why below.

blocks.note: [[Parfois]] and [[quelquefois]] mean the same thing. [[Parfois]] is shorter and more common.

blocks.title: Where the adverb goes
blocks.note: In English the adverb goes **before** the verb (*I often cook*). In French it goes **after** it. With a reflexive verb, it still goes after the verb, not after the pronoun. [[Parfois]] and [[quelquefois]] can also start the sentence.

examples.fr: Nous nous levons toujours à 7 heures.
examples.en: We always get up at 7 o'clock.
Sometimes I get home at 8 p.m.

blocks.title: Never: ne… jamais
blocks.note: **Never** has two parts that wrap around the verb. [[ne]] becomes [[n']] before a vowel. With a reflexive verb, [[ne]] goes before the pronoun. Learn it as a chunk for now; Unit 9 covers negation in full. As a one-word answer, just say [[Jamais !]]

examples.fr: Je ne travaille jamais le dimanche.

examples.en: He never listens to the radio.

examples.fr: Je ne me couche jamais tard.
examples.en: I never go to bed late.
Do you cook in the evening? — Never!

blocks.title: Every day, once a week
blocks.body:
These expressions usually go at the **end** of the sentence, or at the start:

- [[tous les jours]] = every day; [[tous les soirs]] = every evening; [[tous les matins]] = every morning
- [[une fois par semaine]] = once a week; [[deux fois par semaine]] = twice a week; [[une fois par mois]] = once a month

[[Fois]] means *time* in the sense of *one time, two times*. It has nothing to do with clock time ([[l'heure]]).

blocks.title: Le lundi or lundi?
head: French
meaning
rows: On Mondays I work. (every Monday, a habit)
On Monday I work. (this coming Monday, one time)
Every Monday I work. (same as le lundi)
blocks.note: The little word [[le]] turns a day into a **habit**. No article = **one specific** day. This works for every day: [[le samedi]], [[le dimanche]]… And no word for *on*: never [[sur lundi]].

blocks.body:
- **Adverb before the verb:** [[Je souvent cuisine]] ✗ → [[Je cuisine souvent]].
- **Jamais without ne:** [[Je jamais travaille]] ✗ → [[Je ne travaille jamais]].
- **Ne in the wrong place with a reflexive verb:** [[Je me ne lève jamais]] ✗ → [[Je ne me lève jamais]].
- **Every Saturday:** the usual way is [[le samedi]] (singular, with no word for *on*). [[Tous les samedis]] means the same; [[les samedis]] also exists, but [[le samedi]] is the everyday choice.
- **Tous vs toutes:** [[tous les jours]] (jour is masculine), but [[toutes les semaines]] (semaine is feminine).

blocks.title: La fin de semaine
blocks.body:
In Québec and in much of French-speaking Canada, *the weekend* is usually [[la fin de semaine]]. In France it is [[le week-end]]. Both are understood everywhere, and you will hear [[le week-end]] in Québec too.

In relaxed Québec speech you may also hear [[à tous les jours]] or [[à toutes les semaines]], with an extra [[à]]. That is a regional spoken form. In writing, and on the TEF or TCF, use [[tous les jours]].

And in casual speech everywhere, the [[ne]] often disappears: [[Je travaille jamais le dimanche]]. Understand it, but write the [[ne]].

examples.fr: La fin de semaine, je me repose.

blocks.prompt: Answer the survey yourself: say what you do every day, what you do often, what you do sometimes, and what you never do.
checklist: le + a day (le samedi, le lundi…)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Je cuisine tous les jours. Le soir, je regarde souvent la télé. Parfois, je travaille le samedi. Je ne me lève jamais tôt la fin de semaine !
models.en: I cook every day. In the evening, I often watch TV. Sometimes I work on Saturdays. I never get up early on weekends!

blocks.prompt: Write 4 or 5 sentences about your habits for a French class forum. Use at least four different frequency words.
checklist: Put toujours, souvent or rarement after the verb
Use une fois par semaine or tous les jours
Use le + day for a habit

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Je m'appelle Mei. Je cuisine tous les jours. Le samedi, je travaille souvent, mais je ne travaille jamais le dimanche. Le soir, j'écoute toujours la radio. Je regarde rarement la télé. Le mercredi, j'ai un cours de français. Je téléphone à ma mère une fois par semaine.
models.en: My name is Mei. I cook every day. On Saturdays, I often work, but I never work on Sundays. In the evening, I always listen to the radio. I rarely watch TV. On Wednesdays, I have a French class. I call my mother once a week.

summary:
- Say how often with [[toujours, souvent, parfois, rarement]], placed **after** the verb
- Say *never* with [[ne… jamais]] around the verb: [[je ne travaille jamais]]
- Use [[tous les jours]], [[une fois par semaine]], and [[le lundi]] (every Monday) vs [[lundi]] (this Monday)
